prerequisites: Thermodynamic principles, ideal/real gas, vector analysis, differential equations

learning_outcomes.text: Be sensitized to the interacting forces in fluids and the resulting special properties, especially in comparison to solids.
Calculate relevant forces in quiescent compressible and incompressible fluids and quantify static loads.

Analyze all relevant flow variables in geometrically simple flow problems using the streamline/stream tube concept for the one-dimensional description of incompressible frictionless and frictional flows, and design and optimize flow-technical systems using balances.
Be aware of the limits and restrictions of one-dimensional balance calculations and recognize and propose the use of experimental or numerical methods.
Calculate fluid-structure interactions in steady flows using the momentum equation.
Phenomenologically describe boundary layer phenomena and especially turbulence, and formulate solutions for aerodynamic and hydraulic optimization based on this.
Know the advantages and disadvantages of numerical flow calculations and identify possible application areas for solving flow-technical problems.
Numerically analyze geometrically simple flow problems, systematically drawing on preliminary estimates for setting up and parameterizing a simulation.
Design solution strategies to increase the accuracy and efficiency of numerical calculations based on their knowledge of the origin of numerical errors.
Critically question numerical results and check for plausibility using flow hypotheses and balance estimates.
To be able to design and optimize flow-technical products, components, and systems later in relevant industrial sectors such as process engineering, automotive, or energy industry.

syllabus_topics: Properties of fluids, interaction forces in fluids and distinction from solid bodies and point/rigid body mechanics, continuum description
Equation of motion for one-dimensional frictional flows
Special case of quiescent incompressible and compressible fluids:
Hydrostatic fundamental law and technical applications
Pressure profiles in quiescent fluids and resulting force effects
Static buoyancy
Concept of streamline/stream tube for one-dimensional description, deficits and limits of applicability
Description of moving incompressible dissipative fluids with work input or extraction:
Continuity equation
Ideal and extended Bernoulli equation: Concept of control volume, limits of balanced description
Balanced description of turbomachinery
Description of the force effect of steady flows on mechanical structures with help of the momentum equation: Methodological approach, applications
Pipe hydraulics in linear flow systems: Calculation of flow losses in laminar and turbulent flows
Phenomenological description of turbulence and boundary layer effects
Empirical description of bodies in flow using coefficients, airfoil theory and aerodynamics of blunt bodies
Methods for describing and modeling flow processes
Components and procedure of a numerical flow calculation
Discrete description of continuous systems using the finite difference method: Origin and quantification of numerical errors in various discretization methods
Numerical artifacts: Numerical diffusion and stability
Advantages and properties of the Finite Volume Method
Methodical approach to setting up a simulation: Flow hypothesis, selection of a solution method, estimation calculations for parameterizing the solver
Exemplary numerical solution of simple steady and unsteady technical flow problems
Visualization, analysis and extraction of results and identification of numerical problems
assessment_rules: The specific form of examination for MABB411 and MABB412 will be announced at the beginning of the course. A prerequisite for participation in the module examination is successful participation in all offered laboratory work or passing 2 homework assignments (XP) distributed over the semester.
